title: Forecasted Demand Hedging and Contract Flexing Procedure (2026)
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
> **Archived 2026-11-15:** this page is superseded by "Forecasted Demand Hedging and Contract Flexing Procedure" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

This procedure describes how Redwood Inference hedges forecasted demand, flexes contracted capacity commitments, and reconciles invoices against revenue recognition triggers. It sets out the operating principles, decision gates, a runbook for procurement and finance, worked numeric scenarios, and the integration points with the Billing Service and RevRec Engine. The intent is to keep operational flexibility while protecting revenue accounting controls, so neither recognition nor cash position is surprised.

Goals

- Cut the gap between forecasted consumption and committed capacity cost by at least 60% over a 12-month window.
- Keep contract flex changes compliant with revenue recognition rules (the ASC 606 / IFRS 15 analogs implemented in RevRec Engine).
- Give Finance, Procurement, Product and Sales one decision path for commitment adjustments and pricing holdbacks.
- Preserve a clean audit trail for external audit and internal forecasting.

Scope

In scope:
- All committed GPU reservations (Dedicated) and multi-month buy commitments across hosted, dedicated and private products.
- Procurement actions that change monthly committed spend by > $50,000 or capacity by > 10% of the existing commitment.
- Forecast adjustments that move monthly recognized revenue by +/- 5% of forecast.

Out of scope:
- One-off purchase orders under $5,000.
- Non-capacity software licenses with no revenue recognition impact.

Key definitions

- Forecast Hub: the central forecasting dataset and UI used by Finance and Product.
- Commitment Window: the period (usually monthly) covered by a reserved capacity contract.
- Hedging Action: any change that reduces financial exposure to forecast variance (structured discounts, staged ramps, convertible credits).
- Contract Flexing: a formal amendment scaling committed units up or down or adjusting price.
- Pricing Holdback: the part of an invoice deferred or conditioned on future usage milestones to line up with RevRec triggers.

Roles & ownership

- Finance (Forecasting Lead): owns Forecast Hub, produces hedging recommendations, approves accounting impact. Contact: Priya Nambiar.
- Procurement: negotiates amendments and raises POs in ProcureFlow. Contact: Marcus Lee.
- Product: confirms technical capacity needs and rollout timing. Contact: Dana O'Connor.
- Legal: reviews material terms and amendment language. Contact: Arjun Patel.
- Billing Engineering: implements holdbacks and invoice metadata in Billing Service / Commitments API. Contact: Linh Tran.
- RevRec (Accounting Systems): maintains recognition rules in RevRec Engine. Contact: Miguel Santos.

Operating principles

1) Plan procurement on base / expected / upside forecast bands weighted 40/35/25%.
2) When forecast uncertainty exceeds 15% (rolling 90-day MAPE), favour flexibility over the lowest starting unit cost.
3) Every amendment carries amendment_reason, effective_date, capacity_delta, price_delta, pricing_holdback_percent and accounting_treatment (defer/recognize).
4) Any proposed flex that shifts RevRec recognition by > 5% of monthly revenue goes to Finance leadership for pre-approval.

Decision thresholds and gates

- Forecast accuracy SLO: Forecast Hub 30-day MAPE <= 20%. Two consecutive misses trigger a mandatory hedging review.
- Contract flex threshold: capacity_delta >= 10% OR monthly committed cost delta >= $50,000 -> Finance + Procurement + Legal approval required.
- Holdback threshold: pricing_holdback_percent > 10% -> RevRec sign-off required.

Operational procedure

1) Weekly Forecast Review (Finance)
   - Pull the Forecast Hub report: rolling 30/90-day MAPE, p50/p75/p90 demand, open commitments.
   - Raise a Hedging Recommendation if 30-day MAPE > 20% OR p90 demand exceeds committed capacity by > 20% within the next 60 days.

2) Hedging Recommendation (Finance -> Product, Procurement)
   - Lay out options: (A) convert spot to a short-term ramped commit; (B) add staged capacity with a 30-day opt-out; (C) negotiate a convertible credit applied to future overage.
   - Attach estimated P&L impact, RevRec treatment and the scenario model export (.csv).

3) Cross-functional Review Meeting (within 3 business days)
   - Finance forecasting lead, Procurement, Product, Legal, and Sales when customer-facing.
   - Choose an option, assign an owner and timeline, and log it in Forecast Hub as a "Hedging Action ID".

4) Procurement Execution
   - Procurement drafts the amendment in ProcureFlow with metadata pre-filled.
   - Legal reviews and clears final language within 5 business days for standard amendments.
   - Procurement issues the PO / amendment and updates the Commitments API with new capacity and holdback fields.

5) Billing & RevRec Implementation
   - Billing Engineering adds pricing_holdback_percent and holdback_conditions to invoice metadata in Billing Service.
   - RevRec maps the amendment ID to its accounting treatment and recognition schedule in RevRec Engine.
   - Finance checks journal entries in FDW (Finance Data Warehouse) and confirms deferred revenue balances.

6) Monthly Reconciliation (Finance)
   - Match invoices to commitments via the Commitments API: invoice_amount - holdback must equal recognized revenue per the RevRec schedule.
   - Flag any mismatch > 2% of invoice_amount.

7) Post-Implementation Review (30 days after amendment)
   - Compare actual vs modeled cost and forecast variance; record lessons in Forecast Hub against the Hedging Action ID.

Templates & required fields

Procurement amendment metadata:
| field | required | description |
| amendment_id | yes | amend-YYYYMMDD-XXXX |
| amendment_reason | yes | e.g. "hedge demand variance" |
| effective_date | yes | YYYY-MM-DD |
| capacity_delta | yes | integer GPUs, positive or negative |
| price_delta | yes | decimal USD per unit |
| pricing_holdback_percent | conditional | integer 0-100 |
| holdback_conditions | conditional | milestone or usage-based conditions |
| accounting_treatment | yes | "defer" | "recognize" |

Example amendment JSON for the Commitments API
{
  "amendment_id": "amend-20260812-001",
  "effective_date": "2026-09-01",
  "capacity_delta": "+64",
  "price_delta": "-1.25",
  "pricing_holdback_percent": "10",
  "holdback_conditions": "10% held until 30-day cumulative usage >= 80% of new capacity",
  "accounting_treatment": "defer"
}

Accounting impact and controls

- Amendments with accounting_treatment == "defer" must map to a deferred revenue schedule in RevRec Engine, reviewed weekly by accounting until fully recognized.
- Dual review (Finance Lead + Controller) is required for any amendment that raises deferred revenue by > $50,000.
- Each amendment links a Hedging Action ID and the Forecast Hub model export; records are kept for 7 years.

Monitoring, metrics, and SLOs

- Forecast Hub accuracy SLO: 30-day MAPE <= 20% (owner: Finance).
- Reconciliation SLO: monthly mismatch < 2% (owner: Finance Ops).
- Amendment processing SLA: Procurement + Legal signoff on standard templates (owner: Procurement).
- Billing metadata ingestion SLA: new amendment metadata visible in Billing Service within 24 hours of the Commitments API update.

Alerts

- "Forecast Hub MAPE breach": MAPE > 20% for 2 consecutive windows -> auto-create a Hedging Action and notify Finance/Procurement/Product in #finance-procure-alerts.
- "Reconciliation delta": month-end mismatch > 2% -> page Finance Ops on-call and pause further procurement until fixed.

Example scenarios

Scenario A: upside demand
- Committed: $400,000/month for 256 GPUs.
- p90 forecast shows +64 GPUs needed within 45 days (about $120,000/month more).
- Procurement negotiates a staged ramp with 30-day opt-out: +32 GPUs now, +32 after 30 days, pricing_holdback_percent = 10%.
- Month 1 cash outlay rises by $60k with $6k held back and deferred; RevRec Engine recognizes the incremental revenue once the usage milestone is reached.

Scenario B: demand shortfall
- Committed: $300,000/month; near-term usage running -20% vs commit.
- Hedge: convertible credit worth 50% of unused capacity, consumable over the next 90 days or applied to overage at 80% face value.
- Accounting: the credit is contra-revenue when applied, with recognition timing driven by consumption in RevRec Engine.

Governance and escalation

- Disputes between Procurement and Product on technical necessity go to the Head of Platform, who decides capacity need.
- Changes with revenue recognition impact > $500k need Controller and CFO approval before execution.

Rollout checklist (first 90 days)

- Week 0: publish and train Procurement, Finance Ops, Billing Engineering and Legal.
- Week 2: add the amendment metadata schema to ProcureFlow and the Commitments API.
- Week 4: update RevRec Engine staging config for amendment_id mapping.
- Week 6: run an end-to-end simulated amendment and reconciliation.
- Week 12: first post-implementation review and KPI check-in.

Appendix A: Commitments API curl

curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwoodinfra.local/commitments/amendments -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"amendment_id":"amend-20260812-001","effective_date":"2026-09-01","capacity_delta":64,"price_delta":-1.25,"pricing_holdback_percent":10,"accounting_treatment":"defer"}'

Appendix B: Controller audit checklist

- Hedging Action ID and Forecast Hub export attached.
- FDW journal entries match the RevRec schedule.
- Dual approvers recorded for high-value deferrals.
- Signed amendment PDF and legal signoff stored in ProcureFlow.

Document owner and contact

Finance Forecasting Lead: Priya Nambiar (priya.n@redwoodinfra.com). Operational questions: procurement-ops@redwoodinfra.com.
